title: Kingston upon Thames Emergency Help Points
summary: Offline guide to emergency medical help points, urgent care, and local hazards in the Royal Borough of Kingston upon Thames.
content:
For life-threatening emergencies, always dial 999 first (or 112). Call 105 for power cuts and 0800 111 999 for gas leaks.

1. 24-Hour Emergency Hospitals
- Kingston Hospital (24/7 A&E): Galsworthy Road, Kingston upon Thames, KT2 7QB. From Norbiton station: ~4 min walk northeast along Coombe Road and Wolverine Way directly into hospital grounds. From Kingston station: ~15 min walk east via London Road and Coombe Road, or bus 57, 85, 213, or K3.
- St George's Hospital (Nearest Major Trauma Centre): Blackshaw Road, Tooting, SW17 0QT. Accessible via South Western Railway from Kingston/Norbiton to Wimbledon, then bus 493 or 57.

2. Urgent Treatment Centres
- Kingston Urgent Treatment Centre: Ground Floor, Kingston Hospital, Galsworthy Road, KT2 7QB. Integrated with the main hospital emergency admissions entrance.
- Surbiton Health Centre (Out-of-Hours / Same Day): Ewell Road, Surbiton, KT6 6EZ. From Surbiton station: ~10 min walk southeast along Victoria Road and Ewell Road.

3. Local Environmental Hazards
- River Thames (Non-Tidal/Tidal Transition): Fluvial flood risk along the riverside promenades, Lower Ham Road, and Queens Promenade during high upstream discharge.
- Hogsmill River: Active flood corridors and surface water vulnerability running through New Malden, Old Malden, and central Kingston.

4. Essential Supplies
- Major supermarkets and dispensing pharmacies along Clarence Street (Kingston), Victoria Road (Surbiton), and High Street (New Malden) provide bottled water, sanitary goods, and emergency medicine supplies.

Note: addresses and opening hours may have changed — confirm on arrival where possible.
